# Amazon Advertising for Beginners: Is It Worth It for Your Business?
URL: https://factor42media.com/blog/amazon-advertising-for-beginners
Topic: Channels & platforms

Amazon has quietly become one of the largest advertising platforms in the world, and for good reason: it's where enormous numbers of people go specifically to shop and buy. For businesses that sell products, that makes Amazon advertising worth understanding. But it's not right for everyone, and the honest answer to "is it worth it for my business?" depends on what you sell and how. Here's a beginner's guide to what Amazon advertising is and whether it fits you.


## What Amazon advertising is

Amazon advertising means promoting products within Amazon itself — so your products appear when people search and browse on the platform, rather than getting lost among countless listings. When you see sponsored products in Amazon search results or on product pages, that's Amazon advertising at work.

What makes it distinctive is where it reaches people: on a platform they've specifically come to in order to shop. Unlike advertising that interrupts people doing something else, Amazon ads reach people who are actively looking to buy, often with their payment details already saved and their intent to purchase already formed. That shopping-focused context is the heart of Amazon advertising's value.


## Why it can be powerful

Amazon advertising's strength comes from that buying-intent context:

People are there to buy. Amazon shoppers are typically further along toward a purchase than people casually browsing elsewhere. Reaching them can mean reaching customers at the moment of buying intent.

It's an enormous marketplace. The sheer volume of shopping activity on Amazon means a large potential audience for products that fit.

It levels a crowded field. With so many products on Amazon, advertising can be what makes yours visible rather than buried — essential if you're competing for attention among many similar listings.

For the right business, reaching ready-to-buy shoppers on the platform where they shop is a genuinely valuable opportunity.


## Is it worth it for your business?

Here's the honest part: Amazon advertising is worth it for some businesses and irrelevant for others, and the deciding factor is straightforward.

It's likely worth exploring if you sell products, especially products you sell (or could sell) on Amazon, or products that compete in categories where people shop on Amazon. If your business is product-based and your customers shop on Amazon, meeting them there makes sense.

It's probably not for you if you're a local service business, or you sell something that isn't bought on Amazon, or your customers simply aren't shopping there for what you offer. A plumber, a dentist, or a local restaurant gains little from Amazon advertising, because that's not where their customers look for them.

The key question is simply: do your customers shop on Amazon for what you sell? If yes, it's worth considering. If no, your budget belongs on the channels where your customers actually are. Don't chase Amazon because it's big; chase it only if it fits.


## Fitting Amazon into the bigger picture

For businesses where Amazon does fit, it works best as one part of a coordinated marketing effort, not a standalone silo. Amazon advertising can reach shoppers on the platform, but your broader marketing — search, social, and the rest — builds the awareness and brand that make people more likely to choose your product when they see it there. When these work together, they reinforce each other: your other channels build demand, and Amazon captures it at the point of purchase.

That coordination is natural when your marketing is run as one operation and difficult when Amazon is handled as a separate, disconnected effort. Rather than treating Amazon as an island, running it as one coordinated channel — where it fits — lets it work with the rest of your marketing toward the same goals, measured as part of the whole.


## Decide based on fit

Amazon advertising is a powerful way to reach ready-to-buy shoppers — for the businesses whose customers actually shop there. The smart approach is to judge it on fit rather than size: if you sell products your customers buy on Amazon, it's worth exploring as a coordinated part of your marketing; if not, focus your budget where your customers are.

Factor42 Media helps small and mid-sized businesses figure out which channels genuinely fit — and runs the ones that do as part of a coordinated operation from one consolidated place. If Amazon advertising makes sense for your business, we'll run it alongside your other channels toward shared goals; if it doesn't, we'll point your budget where it belongs.

Not sure whether Amazon fits your business? Let's look at it honestly together.

Factor42 Media helps small and mid-sized businesses choose the right channels and run them as a coordinated whole from one consolidated place. Get in touch for honest guidance on where your budget belongs.

# Connecting Your Google Business Profile to Paid Search for Better Results
URL: https://factor42media.com/blog/connecting-google-business-profile-to-paid-search
Topic: Channels & platforms

Two of the most valuable tools a local business has for getting found online are its Google Business Profile — the listing that shows your business on Google's maps and local results — and paid search advertising. Most businesses treat these as entirely separate things. But they work far better together than apart, and connecting them is a straightforward way to get more from both. Here's why they belong together and how coordinating them improves your results.


## The two tools, briefly

Your Google Business Profile is your business's presence in Google's local and map results — the listing showing your name, location, hours, reviews, and details when people search for businesses like yours nearby. It's foundational for local visibility and often the first impression a nearby customer gets. It's part of the unpaid, organic side of being found.

Paid search advertising is when you pay to appear in search results for relevant queries — capturing people actively searching for what you offer, at the moment of intent. It's the paid side, giving you control over when and where you appear.

Both help customers find your business through search, but they do it differently — one through your organic local presence, the other through paid placement. Used together, they cover more of the search landscape than either alone.


## Why connecting them helps

When your Google Business Profile and your paid search work in coordination rather than isolation, several benefits emerge:

You appear more completely. Coordinating your paid and organic search presence means you show up more thoroughly when people search for your business or your category — a stronger, more complete presence than either provides alone.

They reinforce each other. A strong Business Profile makes your paid search more credible and effective, and paid search can drive attention that benefits your overall presence. The two build on each other.

Consistent information builds trust. When your Business Profile and your search advertising present consistent, accurate information about your business, that consistency builds the trust that both search engines and customers reward.

You capture more of the search opportunity. Together, they let you be present across more of the ways people search — organic local results and paid placements — capturing customers you might miss with just one.

The point is that these tools were never meant to be strangers. Coordinated, they form a stronger search presence than the sum of their separate parts.


## The consistency that ties it together

A key benefit of connecting these tools is consistency. Your business information — name, location, offerings, the impression you present — should be accurate and consistent across your Business Profile, your paid search, and everywhere else you appear. That consistency helps customers trust you and helps search engines understand and favor you.

Inconsistency does the opposite: conflicting information across your organic and paid presence confuses customers and undermines the trust that drives visibility. Keeping everything aligned — the same accurate, consistent presence across your Business Profile, your search ads, and your broader online footprint — is what ties your search presence into a coherent whole rather than disconnected pieces.


## Why this points to coordinated marketing

Connecting your Google Business Profile and paid search is really a specific example of a broader principle: your marketing works better when its pieces are coordinated rather than run in isolation. And coordinating them well — keeping information consistent, making them reinforce each other, presenting a coherent search presence — is easiest when your marketing is run as one operation rather than scattered across separate hands.

When one team manages your local presence, your paid search, and your broader marketing together, coordinating your Business Profile and paid search happens naturally, as part of keeping your whole online presence consistent and mutually reinforcing. When these are handled by separate, disconnected providers, the coordination and consistency that make them stronger together tend to fall through the cracks. Getting the full value of connecting your search tools points, like so much else, toward running your marketing as a coordinated whole.


## Make your search presence work together

Your Google Business Profile and your paid search advertising are both valuable for getting found — and they're more valuable coordinated than isolated. Connecting them, and keeping your business information consistent across both and everywhere else, builds a stronger, more complete, more trustworthy search presence that captures more of the customers looking for you.

Factor42 Media manages your local presence, paid search, and broader marketing together from one consolidated place — keeping everything coordinated and consistent so your search tools reinforce each other and your whole online presence works as one. We help you get the full value of every piece by making them work together.

Your search tools are stronger together. Let's connect them and strengthen how customers find you.

Factor42 Media helps small and mid-sized businesses build a coordinated, consistent search presence — Business Profile, paid search, and more — from one consolidated place. Get in touch to strengthen how customers find you.

# Device ID Targeting: Precision Advertising for Small Business
URL: https://factor42media.com/blog/device-id-targeting
Topic: Channels & platforms

Among the many targeting tools in digital advertising, device ID targeting is one of the more precise — and one of the more misunderstood. The name sounds technical and maybe a little intimidating, but the concept is straightforward, and for the right business it offers a level of precision that can make a limited ad budget work much harder. Here's a plain explanation of what it is and when it's useful.


## What device ID targeting is

Every smartphone and tablet carries an advertising identifier — a device ID — that allows ads to be directed to that specific device. Device ID targeting uses these identifiers to reach particular devices (and therefore the people who carry them) with your advertising, rather than broadcasting to a broad, undefined audience.

In practical terms, it means your ads can be aimed with precision at specific devices that meet criteria you care about — reaching a defined set of people on the phones and tablets they carry everywhere. It's one of the tools that makes modern digital advertising far more targeted than the spray-and-pray advertising of the past.


## Why precision matters for a small budget

The value of precise targeting like this is greatest exactly when budgets are tightest — which is to say, for small businesses. When you have limited dollars, you can't afford to waste them reaching people who will never become customers. Every dollar spent on the wrong audience is a dollar gone.

Precise targeting flips that. By reaching specific, relevant devices rather than a broad crowd, more of your budget goes toward people who actually matter to your business. Precision is how a small budget competes with a big one — not by outspending, but by wasting far less. Tools like device ID targeting are part of how a small business advertises smart instead of just advertising loud.


## Where it fits

Device ID targeting is particularly useful for businesses that want to reach specific, well-defined audiences with precision — whether based on behaviors, locations they've visited, or other meaningful criteria. It can also connect to location-based approaches, reaching the devices of people who have been to certain places relevant to your business.

Like any single targeting tool, though, device ID targeting is a tactic, not a whole strategy. It's one precise instrument in a larger toolkit, and its real value emerges when it's used as part of a thoughtful, coordinated marketing effort rather than as an isolated trick. On its own, it reaches specific devices; coordinated with your other channels, the people it reaches can be followed up and reinforced across your whole marketing, turning precise reach into real results.


## Precision without the complexity

Here's the practical concern: tools like device ID targeting are powerful but technical, and a small business owner shouldn't have to become an expert in the plumbing of digital targeting to benefit from it. Figuring out these tactics alone, and coordinating them with everything else, is exactly the kind of complexity that overwhelms busy owners.

This is where running your marketing as one consolidated operation makes the difference. Precise targeting tools like device ID become part of what your team handles for you — used appropriately where they fit, coordinated with your other channels, and measured as part of the whole — without you needing to master the technical details or manage them as separate pieces. You get the precision without the complexity landing on your plate.


## Advertise smart, not just loud

Device ID targeting is one of the tools that lets a small business advertise with precision — reaching specific, relevant devices rather than wasting budget on a broad crowd. Used well, as part of a coordinated marketing effort, it helps a limited budget perform like a larger one by ensuring more of it reaches the right people.

Factor42 Media uses precise targeting tools like device ID as part of your consolidated marketing operation — applying them where they fit, coordinating them with your other channels, and handling the technical complexity so you don't have to. We help your budget reach the right people with precision, all as part of one coordinated plan.

Precision is how a small budget punches above its weight. Let's put the right targeting tools to work for your business.

Factor42 Media helps small and mid-sized businesses reach the right audiences with precise targeting, coordinated across every channel from one consolidated place. Get in touch to make your budget reach the right people.

# Digital Audio: The Overlooked Channel That Reaches Customers Everywhere
URL: https://factor42media.com/blog/digital-audio
Topic: Channels & platforms

When small businesses plan their marketing, they think about search, social, maybe video. One channel that rarely makes the list — but often should — is digital audio: advertising on streaming music services, podcasts, and internet radio. It's overlooked precisely because it's not visual and not flashy, but digital audio reaches people in moments and places no other channel can, often with less competition. Here's why this quiet channel deserves a look.


## What digital audio is

Digital audio advertising means ads delivered through the audio people listen to online — streaming music services, podcasts, digital radio. When you hear an ad between songs on a streaming service or during a podcast, that's digital audio advertising. It reaches people through their ears rather than their eyes, in the audio content they're already choosing to listen to.

What makes it distinct is the context of listening. People consume audio in situations where they can't look at a screen — driving, exercising, cooking, working, commuting. Digital audio reaches them in exactly those moments, when other advertising can't get to them at all. That's the channel's quiet superpower: presence in the parts of your customers' day that visual channels simply can't touch.


## Why digital audio reaches people everywhere

The great advantage of audio is that people listen while doing other things, which means it reaches them across their whole day, including moments no screen-based channel can:

- While driving — a captive audience with no screen to compete for attention.
- While exercising — earbuds in, fully engaged with the audio.
- While working or doing chores — audio playing in the background of tasks throughout the day.
- While commuting — time otherwise unreachable by visual advertising.

In all these moments, people are listening but not looking, and digital audio meets them there. It extends your reach into hours of your customers' lives that visual advertising misses entirely. For a business trying to stay present across a customer's whole day, audio fills gaps nothing else can.


## Why it's overlooked — and why that's an opportunity

Digital audio gets overlooked mostly because it's not visual and not trendy. It doesn't produce eye-catching creative to admire, it's harder to picture than a display ad or a video, and it's simply not top of mind for most small businesses. So they skip it.

But that very overlooked-ness is an opportunity. Because fewer businesses prioritize digital audio, it can be less crowded and competitive than the channels everyone piles onto — potentially meaning better value and more attention for the businesses that do use it. The channel your competitors ignore is often the one where you can stand out affordably. Digital audio's low profile is exactly why it can be a smart, efficient addition for a business willing to look past the obvious channels.


## Making audio work as part of the mix

Like any single channel, digital audio delivers its full value as part of a coordinated marketing effort rather than a standalone experiment. On its own, it reaches people in audio moments — valuable, but limited. Coordinated with your other channels, it becomes more powerful: the awareness it builds during someone's commute or workout can be reinforced when they're later on their phone or computer, and audio fills the gaps in a presence that spans the customer's whole day.

This coordination is natural when your marketing is run as one operation, where digital audio can be added as one channel in a unified plan — reaching people in their listening moments, coordinated with everything else, measured as part of the whole. Rather than a disconnected experiment you're unsure how to evaluate, audio becomes a smart, coordinated extension of your reach. That's how a small business captures the value of this overlooked channel without it becoming another separate thing to manage.


## Reach the moments others miss

Digital audio is an overlooked channel that reaches customers in the parts of their day no visual advertising can touch — driving, exercising, working, commuting — often with less competition than the crowded channels everyone else chooses. For a business wanting to stay present across a customer's whole day, and to do it efficiently, audio is worth a serious look.

Factor42 Media runs digital audio as one coordinated channel in your consolidated marketing operation — reaching customers in their listening moments and reinforcing that reach across everything else, all from one place. We help you capture the value of the channels others overlook, coordinated with the rest of your marketing.

Your customers are listening in moments other ads can't reach. Let's make sure your business is there too.

Factor42 Media helps small and mid-sized businesses reach customers across every channel — including overlooked ones like digital audio — from one consolidated place. Get in touch to expand where your business shows up.

# Digital Out-of-Home Is Now Affordable for Small Business — If You Buy It Right
URL: https://factor42media.com/blog/dooh-is-now-affordable
Topic: Channels & platforms

The billboard has always been the symbol of advertising you couldn't afford. Big, expensive, reserved for major brands, locked up in long contracts — a classic small-business no-go. But out-of-home advertising has gone digital, and in doing so it has quietly become accessible to businesses that could never have considered it before. Digital out-of-home — DOOH — puts your business on screens in the physical world, affordably and flexibly, if you buy it the right way. Here's what it is and how to approach it.


## What DOOH actually is

Digital out-of-home is advertising on digital screens in physical spaces — the screens you pass in shopping centers, gyms, offices, transit stops, gas stations, elevators, restaurants, and along roadways. It's the modern, digital evolution of the old static billboard and poster.

The "digital" part is what changes everything. Because these are digital screens served through digital systems, DOOH can be bought and targeted the way online advertising is — by location, by time of day, flexibly and in smaller increments — rather than through the expensive, rigid, long-term contracts that defined traditional outdoor advertising. That flexibility is exactly what brings it within a small business's reach.


## Why it's affordable now — with a catch

DOOH has become accessible to small businesses because the digital buying model removes the old barriers. You don't need to commit to an enormous, long-term billboard contract. You can target specific screens in specific places at specific times, buying the exposure that's relevant to you without paying for a fortune's worth you don't need. The cost of reaching people on physical-world screens has come down to earth.

But there's a real catch in the "if you buy it right." DOOH is affordable and effective when it's bought smartly and targeted well — the right screens, the right locations, the right timing, coordinated with the rest of your marketing. Bought carelessly, any channel wastes money, and DOOH is no exception. The affordability is real, but capturing it requires buying with some know-how rather than just putting an ad on a screen and hoping. This is the difference between DOOH working for a small business and DOOH being a costly novelty.


## What DOOH does that screens-in-hand can't

DOOH offers something your online channels fundamentally can't: it reaches people in the physical world, in public, with an ad they can't scroll past, close, or block.

While so much advertising fights for attention on personal screens that people are actively trying to ignore, DOOH meets people out in the world — near where they shop, work, and move through their day. Consumers tend to view these ads relatively favorably compared to more intrusive formats, and for a local business, a screen near your location or in the areas your customers frequent can drive real awareness and foot traffic. It reaches customers in the moments they're not on their phones, which is a genuinely different and complementary kind of presence.


## Why buying it right means buying it coordinated

The key to DOOH delivering its value — buying it right — points directly to running it as part of a coordinated marketing effort rather than a standalone billboard buy. When DOOH is targeted thoughtfully and coordinated with your other channels, it becomes far more powerful: the awareness it builds in the physical world can be reinforced by your online channels, and the people who encounter you on a screen can be reached again through search, social, and the rest.

That coordination and smart buying are exactly what a consolidated marketing operation provides. Rather than figuring out DOOH alone and risking a careless buy, it becomes one channel in a unified plan — bought well, targeted properly, coordinated with everything else, and measured as part of the whole. That's how a small business captures DOOH's affordability and impact instead of wasting money on screens.


## Put your business in the physical world

Digital out-of-home has opened the physical-world screen to small businesses — affordable, flexible, and capable of reaching people where online ads can't. The opportunity is real, provided you buy it right: targeted well and coordinated with the rest of your marketing rather than bought blind.

Factor42 Media runs DOOH as one coordinated channel in your consolidated marketing operation — bought smartly, targeted to the right places and times, and working together with your online channels, all from one place. We help you capture the affordability and impact of physical-world screens without the risk of a careless buy.

Ready to put your business out in the world where your customers actually are? Let's do it the right way.

Factor42 Media helps small and mid-sized businesses run digital out-of-home alongside every other channel from one consolidated place — bought smartly and coordinated with the rest of your marketing. Get in touch to reach customers in the physical world.

# Display Advertising That Gets Noticed: Six Best Practices
URL: https://factor42media.com/blog/display-advertising-that-gets-noticed
Topic: Channels & platforms

Display advertising — the banner and image ads that appear across websites and apps — is one of the most widely used forms of digital advertising, and one of the most widely ignored by the people it's shown to. The web is full of display ads that no one notices, remembers, or acts on. Getting your display advertising noticed, in a landscape where people have learned to tune ads out, takes deliberate effort. Here are six best practices for display advertising that actually gets noticed.


## 1. Lead with strong, clear visuals

Display advertising is a visual medium, and in the split second you have to catch someone's attention, the visual does most of the work. Strong, clear, eye-catching visuals are what stop a wandering eye. Cluttered, dull, or confusing visuals get skipped past instantly.

The best display ads are visually clean and immediately appealing — one clear image or design that registers at a glance, rather than a busy jumble competing with itself. In an environment where people barely glance at ads, the visual has to earn that glance and make it count.


## 2. Communicate one clear message

A display ad has room for only one idea done well. Trying to say several things results in an ad that says nothing clearly. Pick the single most important message — one offer, one benefit, one appeal — and make it unmistakable.

The discipline of one clear message is what separates ads that communicate from ads that confuse. A viewer glancing at your ad for a moment should grasp the one thing you want them to know, instantly. Anything more is lost.


## 3. Give people a reason to care

Getting noticed isn't just about catching the eye — it's about catching interest. Your ad needs to quickly convey something the viewer actually cares about: a benefit, an offer, a solution to a problem, a reason to be interested. An ad that just shows your name gives no reason to engage; an ad that offers something relevant earns attention.

Put yourself in the viewer's position: why should they care about this ad in the half-second they see it? Answer that question in the ad itself, and you'll get noticed for the right reasons.


## 4. Include a clear call to action

An ad that gets noticed but gives no next step wastes the attention it captured. Tell viewers clearly what to do — a clear, simple call to action that turns their momentary interest into a step toward becoming a customer. Without it, even a noticed ad often leads nowhere.

The call to action should be obvious and easy to act on, converting the attention your visuals and message earned into actual results.


## 5. Keep it consistent with your brand

Display ads work better when they look and feel like the rest of your marketing — same brand, same style, same message. Consistency makes your ads recognizable and builds on the impression your other channels create, so a viewer who's encountered your brand elsewhere connects the dots. Inconsistent, off-brand ads waste that reinforcing power and can even confuse.

Consistency across your display ads and your other channels turns scattered impressions into cumulative recognition — which is far more powerful than disconnected one-off ads.


## 6. Coordinate display with your other channels

The sixth best practice ties the others together: run your display advertising as part of a coordinated marketing effort, not in isolation. Display ads that reinforce and are reinforced by your other channels get noticed more and work harder — the viewer who saw your streaming ad or social post recognizes your display ad, and the whole becomes more effective than the parts.

This coordination is natural when your marketing is run as one operation and difficult when display is handled separately from everything else. Running your marketing as a coordinated whole means your display advertising is consistent with, and reinforced by, all your other channels — getting noticed more and converting better because it's part of a unified presence rather than a stray ad floating alone. The best display practice of all is not treating display as a standalone thing.


## Get noticed, get results

Display advertising that gets noticed leads with strong visuals, communicates one clear message, gives people a reason to care, includes a clear call to action, stays consistent with your brand, and — tying it together — is coordinated with the rest of your marketing. In a landscape where most display ads are ignored, these practices are what get yours seen and acted on.

Factor42 Media runs display advertising that gets noticed — strong, clear, on-brand, and coordinated with every other channel — all from one consolidated place. We make sure your display ads don't just add to the noise, but actually capture attention and drive results as part of a unified whole.

Tired of display ads no one notices? Let's make yours impossible to ignore.

Factor42 Media helps small and mid-sized businesses run effective, coordinated display advertising across every channel from one consolidated place. Get in touch to get your ads noticed.

# Email Marketing Still Returns $36 for Every $1 — Here's How to Capture It
URL: https://factor42media.com/blog/email-still-returns-36-for-every-1
Topic: Channels & platforms

In a marketing world obsessed with the newest channels and flashiest tactics, one of the highest-returning tools available to a small business is also one of the oldest and least glamorous: email. It doesn't trend. It doesn't come up at conferences much. And it quietly outperforms nearly everything else on return for the money spent.

The often-cited figure is striking: email marketing returns something on the order of $36 for every $1 spent — a return most other channels can only dream of. Yet many small businesses underuse it, neglect it, or treat it as an afterthought. Here's why email works so well and how to actually capture that return.


## Why email returns so much

Email's remarkable return isn't an accident. It comes from a fundamental advantage no advertising channel can match: with email, you're reaching people who have already raised their hands.

An ad interrupts a stranger who may or may not care. An email reaches someone who gave you their address — a customer, a lead, someone who already showed interest in your business. You're not paying to find and persuade cold prospects; you're communicating with people who already know you and chose to hear from you. That warm relationship is why email converts so well and costs so little. You're nurturing existing interest rather than buying new attention, and nurturing is far cheaper and far more effective.

There's also the matter of ownership. Your email list is an asset you own outright — unlike your following on any platform, which lives at the mercy of someone else's algorithm and rules. The people on your list are yours to reach, directly, whenever you have something worth saying. That direct, owned relationship is rare and valuable.


## Why so many businesses leave the return on the table

If email is so effective, why do so many small businesses underuse it? A few reasons, all fixable:

- It's not exciting. Email lacks the novelty of newer channels, so it gets neglected in favor of shinier things — even though it quietly outperforms them.
- It feels like work. Building a list and sending thoughtful, regular emails takes consistent effort, and busy owners let it slide.

It's treated as separate. Email often gets run in isolation from the rest of a business's marketing, as a standalone tool rather than a coordinated part of the whole — which limits how much it can do.

The list is underused as an asset. Many businesses have an email list they barely send to, leaving a valuable, owned audience largely untapped.

The return is there for the taking. Most businesses just don't take it, which is precisely the opportunity for those who do.


## How to actually capture the return

Capturing email's return comes down to a few sound practices:

Build and value your list. Treat your email list as the asset it is — grow it deliberately by giving people good reasons to subscribe, and recognize that every address is a person who's chosen a direct line to your business.

Send things worth opening. The return comes from communicating value, not blasting your list. Useful, relevant, welcome messages keep people engaged; noise makes them leave.

Be consistent. Email rewards a steady presence — staying in touch so your business stays top of mind for the customers and leads who already know you.

Coordinate it with everything else. This is the big one. Email works best not as a standalone silo but as a connected part of your whole marketing, working with your other channels.

That last point is where most of the untapped return hides.


## Why email works best when it's not alone

Email run in isolation is good. Email coordinated with the rest of your marketing is far better — and this is where consolidation multiplies its value.

When email is connected to your other channels, powerful things happen. The people who engage with your ads can flow onto your email list. The customers on your list can be reached again through your other channels for reinforcement. What you learn about your audience in one channel informs your email, and vice versa. Email stops being a standalone tool and becomes part of a coordinated system where every channel feeds the others. That coordination — impossible when email is run by a separate vendor in its own silo — is exactly what a consolidated setup makes natural, and it's how you capture email's full return rather than just part of it.


## Don't leave $36 on the table

Email marketing quietly offers one of the best returns in all of marketing, reaching people who already want to hear from you, through a channel you actually own. Underusing it is leaving money on the table — money that's unusually easy to pick up.

Factor42 Media runs email as a coordinated part of your whole marketing operation from one consolidated place — connected to your ads, your social, and every other channel so it delivers its full return rather than sitting in a silo. We help you build your list, treat it as the asset it is, and put it to work alongside everything else.

Email still returns $36 for every $1. Let's make sure your business is actually capturing it.

Factor42 Media helps small and mid-sized businesses capture the full return of email by running it alongside every other channel from one consolidated place. Get in touch to put your email list to work.

# Finding Your Niche With Streaming Audio and Podcast Ads
URL: https://factor42media.com/blog/finding-your-niche-with-audio
Topic: Channels & platforms

Not all advertising is about reaching the most people — sometimes it's about reaching exactly the right people. Streaming audio and podcast advertising are particularly good at this, because the audio content people choose reveals a lot about who they are and what they care about. For a business trying to reach a specific niche audience, podcasts and streaming audio offer a precision that broad channels can't match. Here's how to find your niche through audio.


## Why audio is good for niche targeting

The power of podcasts and streaming audio for niche marketing comes from a simple truth: people choose audio content that reflects their specific interests, passions, and identities. Someone who listens to a podcast about a particular hobby, industry, or interest has told you something meaningful about themselves just by choosing it. The content people listen to is a strong signal of who they are.

This makes audio — especially podcasts — a precise way to reach niche audiences. There are podcasts and audio content for nearly every interest, community, and niche imaginable, and their listeners are often deeply engaged with the subject. Advertising within content that matches your target niche reaches exactly the people most likely to care about what you offer, at a moment when they're engaged with a topic related to it. That precision is hard to achieve through broad channels.


## The engaged-audience advantage

Beyond precise targeting, podcast and audio audiences bring another advantage: engagement and trust. People often develop real relationships with the podcasts and audio content they follow — listening regularly, trusting the hosts, feeling part of a community. This engaged, trusting context can rub off on the advertising within it, giving your message a more receptive audience than it might find in a more distracted, skeptical environment.

For a niche business, reaching a small but highly engaged and relevant audience is often far more valuable than reaching a large but indifferent one. Audio's combination of precise niche targeting and engaged audiences is exactly suited to businesses whose ideal customers form a specific, identifiable group rather than a broad mass.


## Is niche audio right for your business?

Streaming audio and podcast advertising is especially valuable if:

Your customers form a specific niche — a particular interest, community, industry, or identity — rather than a broad, general audience. Audio's precision shines when there's a defined group to reach.

There's audio content matching your niche — podcasts or streaming audiences organized around the interests your customers share, which for most niches, there are.

You value engaged relevance over broad reach — reaching the right, engaged people matters more to your business than reaching the most people.

If these describe your business, niche audio could be a smart, precise way to reach your ideal customers. If your customers are more of a broad general audience, other channels may serve better — the point is matching the channel to your situation.


## Making niche audio work in your mix

As with any channel, niche audio delivers its full value as part of a coordinated marketing effort rather than a standalone play. Reaching your niche through podcasts is powerful; reinforcing that reach across your other channels — so the people you reach through relevant audio encounter your business again elsewhere — is more powerful still. Audio finds and engages your niche; coordination with your other channels deepens and converts that engagement.

This coordination is natural when your marketing is run as one operation, where niche audio can be added as one precisely-targeted channel in a unified plan — reaching your specific audience and working with everything else, measured as part of the whole. Rather than an isolated experiment, niche audio becomes a coordinated tool for reaching and winning your ideal customers. That's how a business captures audio's niche-targeting power as part of a coherent whole.


## Reach exactly the right people

Streaming audio and podcast advertising offer a precise way to reach niche audiences — because the audio people choose reveals their specific interests, and its listeners are often deeply engaged. For a business whose ideal customers form an identifiable group, audio can reach exactly the right people, in an engaged and trusting context, coordinated with the rest of your marketing.

Factor42 Media runs niche audio as one coordinated channel in your consolidated marketing operation — reaching your specific audience through relevant podcasts and streaming, and reinforcing that reach across everything else, all from one place. We help you find and win your niche as part of a coordinated whole.

Your ideal customers are listening to content that reflects exactly who they are. Let's reach them there.

# From Search to Streaming TV: Running All Your Ads Under One Roof
URL: https://factor42media.com/blog/from-search-to-streaming-tv-one-roof
Topic: Channels & platforms

Think about everywhere your business might want to show up. Someone searches Google for what you sell — you want to be there. They scroll Instagram — you want to be there too. They watch a streaming show on their living room TV, listen to a podcast, browse websites, pass a digital billboard, check their email. Each of those is a place a potential customer's attention lives, and each is a channel your marketing could occupy.

The modern reality is that customers are spread across an enormous range of channels, and reaching them means being on many of them. The question isn't whether to be multi-channel — it's how to run all those channels without it becoming an unmanageable mess. The answer is to run them under one roof.


## The span of channels a business needs today

It's worth appreciating just how wide the modern channel landscape is, because it explains why the old ways of managing marketing break down. A business that wants to meet its customers where they are might reasonably want to be on:

- Search — capturing active intent when people look for what you offer.
- Paid social — Facebook, Instagram, and the platforms where attention lives.
- Streaming TV — the living-room screen, now reachable affordably as viewing shifts to streaming.
- Programmatic display — your brand across the websites your customers browse.
- Email — direct connection to the customers and leads you already have.
- Newer channels — Reddit, TikTok, digital out-of-home, and others reaching audiences the staples miss.

That's a lot of ground. Covering it is how you reach customers across their whole day rather than catching them in just one moment. But covering it the wrong way — a separate vendor or a separate late-night effort for each — creates exactly the fragmentation that makes marketing miserable and wasteful.


## Why "under one roof" beats "one vendor per channel"

The instinct, faced with many channels, is to assign each to a specialist. Search to a search vendor, social to a social agency, and so on. It feels organized. It isn't. It scatters your marketing across providers who each see only their piece, charge their own fee, report their own way, and never coordinate. You get breadth at the cost of coherence — many channels, no strategy, and you stuck in the middle holding it together.

Running everything under one roof — one team handling all the channels together — gives you the breadth and the coherence. The same range of channels, but planned as one, run by one team, coordinated toward one goal. The difference is enormous and shows up in three ways.


## What one roof makes possible

Coordination across the whole span. When search and streaming and social and email are run by one team that sees them all, they work together. The person who saw your streaming ad can be reached on social; the search clicker can be added to your email nurture; budget can flow to whatever's performing best across the entire mix. Under separate roofs, every channel operates blind to the others. Under one, they reinforce each other.

One clear picture instead of many. All those channels, measured the same way, in one view. You can finally see how your whole marketing is doing and which parts are earning their keep — impossible when each channel reports separately in its own format.

One relationship, one bill, far less cost. One team means one point of contact, one report, and one fee instead of a stack of vendor invoices each carrying its own overhead. Collapsing the duplication is why running everything under one roof can cost dramatically less — often more than 70% less than juggling separate vendors or paying a full-service agency — while covering more ground, not less.


## Breadth without the burden

The goal was never to be on fewer channels. Your customers are everywhere, and reaching them means being everywhere they are — from search to streaming TV and beyond. The goal is to achieve that breadth without the burden that usually comes with it: the scattered vendors, the fragmented reporting, the coordination falling on you, the cost multiplying with every channel added.

Factor42 Media runs your entire span of channels under one roof — search, social, programmatic, email, streaming TV, DOOH, and the rest — as a single coordinated operation from one place. All the reach of a full multi-channel presence, none of the fragmentation, at a cost far below the scattered alternative. Adding a channel doesn't mean adding a vendor; it just means one more part of the same coordinated plan.

Every place your customers are, your business can be — all run under one roof. Let's cover the whole map together.

# Geo-Fencing Explained: Reaching Customers at the Right Place and Time
URL: https://factor42media.com/blog/geo-fencing-explained
Topic: Channels & platforms

Some marketing ideas sound more complicated than they are. Geo-fencing is one of them. The name conjures something technical and intimidating, but the concept is refreshingly simple, and for the right business it's one of the more clever ways to reach potential customers exactly where and when it matters. Here's a plain-English explanation of what geo-fencing is, how it works, and whether it's worth it for your business.


## What geo-fencing actually is

Geo-fencing means drawing a virtual boundary around a real-world location and showing ads to people while they're inside it. That's the whole idea. You pick a geographic area — a neighborhood, a shopping center, a competitor's location, an event venue — and people who enter that area can be served your ads on their phones.

Think of it as an invisible fence around a place that matters to your business. When someone crosses into it, they become reachable with your message. Instead of advertising to a broad, scattered audience, you're reaching people based on where they physically are — which, for many businesses, is a powerful signal of what they might want right now.


## Why location is such a useful signal

The reason geo-fencing works is that physical location often reveals intent in a way little else can. Where someone is says a lot about what they might be interested in at that moment.

Someone inside a shopping district is in a shopping mindset. Someone at a home improvement store might be a prospect for related services. Someone attending a particular event has told you something about their interests just by being there. Someone near your competitor's location is, quite possibly, in the market for exactly what you offer. Geo-fencing lets you turn these real-world locations into targeting, reaching people at the moment their physical presence suggests they're most receptive. It's advertising aimed by place and timing, which for local and location-driven businesses is often far more relevant than broad demographic targeting.


## What businesses geo-fencing suits

Geo-fencing isn't for everyone, but it's especially powerful for certain kinds of businesses:

- Local businesses wanting to reach people in their immediate area at the moment they're nearby.
- Businesses near competitors, who can reach potential customers while they're literally at a competitor's location, making the case to choose them instead.
- Event-driven businesses, reaching attendees of relevant events, conferences, or gatherings.
- Location-specific services, where being physically near a certain type of place signals a real need.

If your business benefits from reaching people based on where they are — and many local businesses do — geo-fencing is worth serious consideration. If your customers are defined more by who they are than where they are, other targeting may serve you better. The point is to match the tool to your situation.


## Where geo-fencing fits in the bigger picture

Here's the important context: geo-fencing is a tactic, not a whole marketing strategy. It's one clever tool for reaching people by location, and it works best as part of a coordinated marketing effort rather than a standalone trick.

On its own, a geo-fencing campaign reaches people in a location — useful, but limited. Coordinated with your other channels, it becomes far more powerful: the people you reach through geo-fencing can be followed up on social or search, reinforced with your other messaging, and folded into your overall picture of what's working. Geo-fencing as an isolated tactic is a nice one-off. Geo-fencing as one coordinated channel among many is a genuine advantage.

This is the difference between bolting on tactics one at a time — which recreates the fragmentation problem — and running every tactic as part of one coordinated plan. A tool like geo-fencing delivers its full value when it's integrated with everything else, not managed as yet another separate thing.


## A smart tool, used well

Geo-fencing is a clever, approachable way to reach customers based on the powerful signal of where they physically are — well-suited to local and location-driven businesses, and best used as one coordinated part of a broader marketing effort rather than an isolated gimmick.

Factor42 Media runs geo-fencing alongside every other channel from one consolidated place, so it works as part of a coordinated plan — reaching people by location and then reinforcing that reach across your other channels, all measured together. We help you use the right tactics for your business and make them work as a system rather than a scattered collection.

If reaching customers at the right place and time sounds valuable for your business, let's talk about how geo-fencing fits into your bigger picture.

Factor42 Media helps small and mid-sized businesses use location-based tactics like geo-fencing as part of a coordinated marketing plan run from one consolidated place. Get in touch to reach customers where it counts.

# Google Discovery Ads: What They Are and Whether They're Worth It
URL: https://factor42media.com/blog/google-discovery-ads
Topic: Channels & platforms

Google offers many advertising formats, and among the ones small business owners hear about but often don't understand are Discovery ads — a format designed to reach people across Google's various feeds as they browse and discover content. Whether they're worth it for your business depends on understanding what they do and how they fit your goals. Here's a plain explanation and an honest assessment.


## What Discovery ads are

Discovery ads are a Google advertising format that shows visually rich ads across Google's feed-based surfaces — the places where people scroll and discover content rather than actively search. Instead of appearing when someone searches for something specific, Discovery ads reach people as they browse, aiming to catch their interest while they're in a discovering, browsing frame of mind.

The distinction from regular search ads matters. Search ads capture people at the moment they're actively looking for something — high intent, ready to act. Discovery ads work more like social media advertising: reaching people who aren't necessarily searching for you but might be interested, catching their attention as they browse. It's a different moment in the customer's mindset, which shapes what Discovery ads are good for.


## What they're good at

Discovery ads have particular strengths:

Building awareness and interest. Because they reach people who are browsing rather than searching, Discovery ads are well-suited to introducing your business to potential customers and sparking interest — the upper parts of the customer journey, before someone is ready to buy.

Visual appeal. They're a visually rich format, so they can showcase your business, products, or brand attractively as people scroll.

Broad reach across Google's surfaces. They can put your business in front of people across the various places they browse within Google's ecosystem.

In short, Discovery ads are more of an awareness-and-interest tool than a capture-ready-buyers tool — good for reaching people earlier in their journey and drawing them toward you.


## Are they worth it for your business?

Whether Discovery ads are worth it depends on your goals and where they'd fit:

They may be worth it if you want to build awareness and interest, reach people who aren't yet searching for you, and draw new potential customers toward your business. For upper-funnel goals, they can be valuable.

They may be less essential if your priority is capturing people already actively searching for what you offer — in which case search ads, which meet high intent directly, might matter more first.

Like most channels and formats, Discovery ads aren't universally right or wrong — they're right for certain purposes. The question isn't "are Discovery ads good?" but "do they fit where I need to reach customers?" For building awareness and interest as part of a broader effort, they can absolutely earn their place.


## Why they work best as part of the whole

Here's the key to getting value from Discovery ads: they work best as one part of a coordinated marketing effort covering the whole customer journey, not as an isolated tactic. Discovery ads are good at the awareness-and-interest stages — but those stages only pay off if the interest they build is captured and converted by your other channels further down the journey.

A Discovery ad that sparks someone's interest is valuable only if that person can then be reached again — through search when they're ready to buy, through social to deepen the relationship, through email to nurture them. Run in isolation, Discovery ads build interest that then leaks away with nothing to catch it. Coordinated with your other channels, they become a powerful top-of-journey tool feeding customers into the rest of your marketing.

This is exactly what running your marketing as one operation provides. Discovery ads as one coordinated channel — building awareness and interest that your other channels then capture and convert — deliver far more than Discovery ads run alone. Whether they're "worth it" often comes down to whether they're part of a coordinated whole that can capitalize on the interest they create.


## Fit them to your journey

Google Discovery ads are a format for reaching people as they browse and discover — good at building awareness and interest, less about capturing ready buyers. Whether they're worth it depends on your goals and, crucially, on whether they're coordinated with the rest of your marketing so the interest they build gets captured and converted.

Factor42 Media runs formats like Discovery ads as coordinated parts of your consolidated marketing operation — building awareness and interest that your other channels then convert, all working together across the customer journey from one place. We help you use the right formats for the right purposes, coordinated into a whole that actually turns interest into customers.

Wondering whether Discovery ads fit your business? Let's look at where they'd fit in your whole marketing.

Factor42 Media helps small and mid-sized businesses use the right ad formats across every channel, coordinated from one consolidated place. Get in touch to build marketing that covers the whole journey.

# How Email Fits Into a Consolidated Marketing Strategy
URL: https://factor42media.com/blog/how-email-fits-into-a-consolidated-strategy
Topic: Channels & platforms

Email is often run as an island. Many businesses treat it as a standalone tool — a separate platform, a separate activity, disconnected from the rest of their marketing. And email works reasonably well even in isolation, which is part of why it stays siloed. But email reaches its full potential only when it's woven into a coordinated marketing strategy, working with your other channels rather than beside them. Here's how email fits into a consolidated approach, and why that fit makes it dramatically more valuable.


## Email's unique role

To understand how email fits, start with what makes it distinct. Email is your direct line to people who already know you — customers and subscribers who've shared their address and chosen to hear from you. It's an owned channel: your list belongs to you, not to a platform's algorithm. And it's one of the highest-return channels in all of marketing, precisely because it reaches warm, interested people directly.

That role — the direct, owned, high-return connection to people who already know you — is email's special contribution to a marketing strategy. It's not trying to reach cold strangers like some channels; it's nurturing and activating the relationships you've already built. Understanding this role is the key to placing email correctly within a broader strategy.


## Where email fits in the customer journey

Email's distinct role gives it a natural place in the customer journey. While some channels excel at building awareness among people who don't know you yet, and others at capturing people at the moment of purchase, email shines in nurturing relationships and driving repeat engagement with people already in your orbit.

Email is where you deepen the relationship after someone first discovers you, keep customers engaged over time, bring people back, and turn one-time buyers into repeat ones. It's the channel of ongoing relationship, not first contact. In a well-designed strategy, your other channels bring people into your world, and email nurtures and retains them — each channel doing what it does best, handing off to the next.


## Why email needs the other channels — and they need it

Here's the crucial insight: email and your other channels make each other more valuable, which is exactly why email shouldn't be an island.

Your other channels feed email. The awareness and interest your search, social, and streaming generate bring new people who can join your email list — so a coordinated setup continuously grows your list rather than letting it stagnate. And email feeds your other channels. What you know about your engaged email audience can inform your advertising, and email can reinforce the messages people encounter elsewhere. The people on your list can be reached across other channels too, for coordinated reinforcement.

Run email in isolation and you lose all of this cross-pollination — the list doesn't grow from your other efforts, and email's insights and reach don't strengthen the rest of your marketing. Run it as part of a coordinated whole, and email and your other channels amplify each other. That mutual reinforcement is worth a great deal, and it's only available when email isn't siloed.


## Why consolidation unlocks email's potential

This is where a consolidated marketing strategy makes the decisive difference. Email delivers its full value when it's connected to everything else — growing from your other channels, informing them, reinforcing them, working as part of a coordinated journey. And that connection is exactly what a consolidated setup provides and a fragmented one prevents.

When your marketing is run as one operation, email is woven into the whole — your channels feed your list, email nurtures the people they bring in, and everything reinforces everything else, coordinated by one team with one view of your customer. When email is run by a separate vendor in its own silo, disconnected from the rest, it can't participate in this cross-channel reinforcement, and its full potential goes unrealized. Getting the most from email — one of your highest-return channels — is one more compelling reason to run your marketing as a coordinated whole rather than a set of disconnected pieces.


## Bring email into the fold

Email is one of the most valuable channels a business has — a direct, owned, high-return line to people who already know you. But run as an island, it delivers only part of its potential. Woven into a consolidated strategy — fed by your other channels, feeding them in return, nurturing customers through a coordinated journey — email becomes dramatically more powerful, and makes your whole marketing stronger.

Factor42 Media runs email as an integral part of your consolidated marketing operation from one place — connected to every other channel, so your list grows from your broader marketing, your email nurtures the relationships they build, and everything reinforces everything else. We help you unlock email's full potential by bringing it into the fold rather than leaving it on an island.

Email is too valuable to leave siloed. Let's weave it into a coordinated strategy where it — and your whole marketing — performs at its best.

# Is SEO Dead? Why Search Optimization Matters More Than Ever
URL: https://factor42media.com/blog/is-seo-dead
Topic: Channels & platforms

Every so often, someone declares SEO dead. Lately the obituaries have grown louder, driven by the rise of AI-powered search and the fear that if AI just answers questions directly, there's no point optimizing to be found. For a small business owner, the confusion is understandable and the stakes are real — you don't want to keep investing in something obsolete, nor abandon something that still works. So let's answer the question honestly: is SEO dead? No — but it is changing, and understanding how helps you invest your effort wisely.


## Where the "SEO is dead" idea comes from

The death-of-SEO talk isn't coming from nowhere. Search is genuinely changing. AI-powered tools increasingly answer questions directly, sometimes without sending people to any website. For certain kinds of broad, informational queries, this really does reduce the clicks that businesses used to earn by ranking well. If your entire SEO strategy depended on ranking for general informational questions and capturing that traffic, you're feeling real pressure, and the "SEO is dead" narrative resonates.

But "the way SEO used to work for some queries is under pressure" is very different from "SEO is dead." The first is true and worth adapting to. The second is an overstatement that could lead a business to abandon something still valuable.


## Why SEO is far from dead

SEO — the practice of helping your business be found in search — remains valuable for reasons that AI hasn't erased:

People still search constantly. Search remains one of the primary ways people find businesses, products, and services, especially local ones. As long as people search, being findable in search matters.

Local search is resilient. When people look for a local business — a service near them, a place to go, someone to hire — they still turn to search and still need concrete results. This behavior has been far less disrupted by AI, and for local businesses it's the heart of the matter.

AI draws on optimized content. Even AI-powered answers pull from information across the web. Being clear, credible, and well-optimized helps your business be understood and referenced by AI tools, not just traditional search. Good SEO increasingly helps you show up in AI answers too.

Being found is still the whole point. Whatever form search takes, helping customers find your business is essential — and that's what SEO fundamentally does. The goal endures even as the tactics evolve.

Far from dead, SEO is arguably more important as being findable gets more complex — you want expertise ensuring you show up however people are searching.


## What's actually changing

Rather than dying, SEO is evolving, and the smart move is to evolve with it:

- From chasing broad informational traffic to focusing on high-intent and local searches — the searches that lead to actual business and that remain resilient.
- From ranking alone to broader visibility — being found not just in traditional results but in AI answers, maps, and wherever customers look.
- From gaming algorithms to genuine quality — clear, credible, useful information about your business, which serves you across traditional search and AI alike.

These shifts reward businesses that focus on genuinely helping customers find and understand them, and penalize those relying on outdated tricks. That's a healthy evolution, not a death.


## Why coordinated marketing helps here too

Getting found in the evolving search landscape draws on your whole online presence — your website, your local listings, your reviews, your content, your consistency across the web. When these are managed in a scattered way, they're inconsistent, which undermines your search visibility just when it's getting more complex. When they're coordinated, they reinforce each other into the clear, credible, consistent presence that helps you show up — in traditional search, local results, and AI answers alike.

This is a natural benefit of running your marketing as one operation. Your SEO, listings, reviews, content, and broader marketing all working together produce far stronger visibility than any piece managed in isolation. As search gets more complex, that coordination becomes more valuable, not less.


## Don't bury SEO — evolve it

SEO isn't dead. It's evolving, as search itself evolves, toward high-intent and local searches, broader visibility, and genuine quality. Abandoning it because of AI headlines would be a costly mistake; the businesses that keep helping customers find them — through search that's adapted to how people actually look now — will keep getting found.

Factor42 Media helps small and mid-sized businesses stay findable as search evolves — managing SEO alongside listings, reviews, content, and every other channel from one consolidated place, so your whole presence works together to help customers find you across traditional search and AI alike. We help you evolve your search strategy rather than abandon it.

SEO isn't dead — but it does reward doing it right. Let's make sure your customers can still find you.

Factor42 Media helps small and mid-sized businesses stay visible in search — managed alongside every other channel from one consolidated place. Get in touch to keep customers finding you.

# Is TikTok Right for Your Business? A Straight Answer
URL: https://factor42media.com/blog/is-tiktok-right-for-your-business
Topic: Channels & platforms

TikTok generates strong opinions. Some business owners are convinced it's essential; others are sure it's a frivolous place for teenagers that has nothing to do with their business. Both camps are partly right and partly wrong, which is why the honest answer to "is TikTok right for my business?" is: it depends — and here's exactly what it depends on, so you can decide for yourself.


## First, let go of the outdated assumptions

Before you can judge TikTok fairly, drop the stereotype. The idea that TikTok is only dancing teenagers is years out of date. Its audience has broadened enormously — adults across age groups now use it, many of them actively discovering products, services, and local businesses through the app. Its advertising business has grown at a remarkable pace as businesses of all kinds have found it works.

So "my customers aren't on TikTok" is a much weaker assumption than it used to be. For a lot of businesses, the customers are there — the owner just assumed they weren't. Start from the real, current TikTok, not its outdated reputation.


## When TikTok is a strong fit

TikTok tends to work well for businesses with certain characteristics. It's worth a serious look if:

Your business is visual. TikTok is a visual, video-first platform. If what you do can be shown — a product, a space, a transformation, a process, a personality — you have raw material that fits naturally.

Your customers skew toward the TikTok audience. While it's broadened, TikTok still over-indexes with younger and trend-attentive audiences. If that overlaps with your customers, the fit is strong.

You can be authentic and a little creative. TikTok rewards genuine, engaging content over polished, expensive production. If you or someone on your team can show real personality, that's an advantage — and a cost saving, since you don't need a big production budget.

You want to reach people before your competitors do. Many local businesses aren't on TikTok yet, so early movers often find attention that's cheaper and less contested than the crowded older platforms.

If several of these describe your business, TikTok may be a genuine opportunity rather than a distraction.


## When TikTok probably isn't the priority

In fairness, TikTok isn't right for everyone, and it's worth being honest about that too. It may not be your best use of budget if:

- Your business is hard to make visual. Some businesses don't lend themselves to short-form video, and forcing it wastes effort.
- Your customers clearly aren't there. For some narrow or specialized audiences, other channels reach them far more directly.

You have no capacity for the content it requires. TikTok rewards a steady stream of authentic content, and if you truly can't produce that, other channels may serve you better.

The point isn't that TikTok is universally good or bad — it's that it fits some businesses well and others poorly, and knowing which you are saves you from both missing an opportunity and chasing a bad one.


## The real question: where does it fit?

Even if TikTok is a good fit, it shouldn't be a standalone gamble. The smart way to approach it — like any channel — is as one coordinated part of your overall marketing, not an isolated experiment run off to the side.

When TikTok works alongside your other channels — the audience you build there feeding into your broader marketing, its performance measured against everything else, its role coordinated with your search, social, and the rest — you can tell whether it's actually earning its place, and it reinforces the rest of your marketing rather than sitting apart. This is far easier when your marketing is run as one operation, where a channel like TikTok can be added, coordinated, and honestly measured as part of the whole, rather than bolted on as one more separate thing.


## Decide with clear eyes

Is TikTok right for your business? Judge it on the real platform, not the stereotype: consider whether your business is visual, whether your customers are there, whether you can be authentic, and whether you'd be early. If the answers lean yes, it's worth doing — as a coordinated part of your marketing, honestly measured. If they lean no, spend your budget where it fits better.

If TikTok makes sense for your business, we'll run it alongside everything else and measure whether it's truly working; if it doesn't, we'll tell you straight and focus your budget where it belongs.

# Local SEO in the Age of AI: Why Your Business Still Needs to Be Found
URL: https://factor42media.com/blog/local-seo-in-the-age-of-ai
Topic: Channels & platforms

If you run a local business, you've probably heard the anxious talk: artificial intelligence is upending search, AI is answering questions directly, and the old rules of getting found online are crumbling. It's enough to make a small business owner wonder whether local SEO is even worth the effort anymore.

Here's the reassuring reality. AI is genuinely changing search — but local search, the kind that matters most to a business serving a specific area, is among the most resilient corners of the whole landscape. Understanding why will help you focus your effort where it still pays off handsomely, instead of panicking over changes that don't affect you as much as the headlines suggest.


## What AI is actually changing

The big shift is that AI-powered search increasingly answers questions directly. Ask a broad informational question and you may get a generated answer at the top of the page, sometimes without needing to click through to any website at all. For certain kinds of content — general how-to and informational queries — this genuinely changes how people find answers, and businesses that relied on ranking for those broad questions are feeling it.

That's the disruption driving the anxious headlines, and for some types of businesses and content, it's real and worth adapting to. But notice the specific kind of query where AI answers dominate: broad, informational, general-knowledge questions. That's not how people search when they're looking for a local business.


## Why local search is more resilient

When someone needs a local business, they don't search the way they search for general information. They search with local, transactional intent: the plumber near them, a dentist accepting new patients in their town, the best place nearby for what they need right now. These searches are fundamentally different, and they've been far less disrupted by AI answers.

The reason is simple. AI is good at answering general questions, but "which specific local business should I actually go to, and how do I reach it?" isn't a general question — it's a local, practical one that still leads people to maps, listings, reviews, and business websites. When someone's ready to call, visit, or buy from a business near them, they still need the concrete details that local search provides. That behavior has stayed remarkably stable even as broader search evolves. For local businesses, the ground is far steadier than the headlines suggest.


## What still matters for getting found locally

Because local search remains resilient, the fundamentals of local SEO still pay off — arguably more than ever, since some competitors may wrongly neglect them out of AI panic. The things that help customers find a local business still work:

- A strong, complete business listing — accurate name, address, hours, and details, so you show up when people search nearby and can act on what they find.
- Reviews — they influence both whether you appear in local results and whether customers choose you once they see you. They remain powerful.
- Local relevance on your website — clearly signaling where you are and what you do, so search engines and customers alike understand you serve their area.
- Consistency across the web — the same accurate business information everywhere it appears, which builds the trust that local search rewards.
- None of these have been made obsolete by AI. If anything, doing them well is a reliable advantage precisely while others are distracted.


## Don't panic — position

The smart response to AI's effect on search isn't to abandon local SEO; it's to keep doing the fundamentals well while staying aware of the broader shift. A local business that maintains a strong listing, gathers reviews, and keeps its information consistent will continue to be found by the customers who matter — because those customers are searching in exactly the resilient, local, ready-to-act way that AI has changed the least.

There's also an opportunity in the anxiety. As some businesses neglect their local SEO out of confusion about AI, the ones that stay disciplined stand out more. The panic is a chance to gain ground, not lose it.


## Stay found where it counts

AI is reshaping parts of search, but local search — the kind that brings customers to a business serving their area — remains one of the most stable and valuable channels a local business has. The fundamentals still work, the customers are still searching, and the businesses that keep showing up will keep getting found.

Factor42 Media helps local businesses stay found where it counts, managing local SEO alongside every other marketing channel from one consolidated place — so your listings, reviews, and local presence work together with your ads and everything else, all coordinated and all current with how search actually works today.

Don't let AI headlines scare you off the fundamentals. Your customers are still searching for a business like yours. Let's make sure they find you.
